theme_rationale_483: Action #1 = the Irish war is 483's backbone (raids on Cornwall & western Logres, near Hindon's march). Personal #2 = the heir question + the Prince's Passion. Social #3 = court/affinity/Gwythyr. Tension/Mystery rare -- the master-hunt runs on its high-weight threads + Fate, not the theme dial. #1 rotated off Social (rule); Action's first #1 (10-yr coverage).

allocation_rules.reallocate_at: End of each Winter Phase, for the UPCOMING year, by that year's GPC brief + live threads.
constraints: each theme is #1 at least once per ~10 yrs -- TRACKED in theme_history; SOFT-PRESSURE: a theme unused as #1 for ~8 yrs gets priority for the next fitting year
allocation_rules.weighting: 1st 40% (d10 1-4) / 2nd 30% (5-7) / 3rd 20% (8-9) / 4th & 5th ~5% each (10). Only the top 3 are meaningfully present.
allocation_rules.turning_point_triggers: Fire the Adventure-Crafter Turning Point (themes + Lists) at: (a) ALTERED scene-test results; (b) INTERRUPT (Random Event) scenes; AND (c) optionally at any scene-start with NO clear Expected Scene ('what happens next?') -- pull from the Lists / roll a Turning Point to generate the next scene. This surfaces themes + the high-weight GPC threads OFTEN, not just on rare Altered results.

gpc_seeding.rule: At each Winter Phase, seed the UPCOMING year's key GPC events as THREADS and key NPCs as CHARACTERS, tagged gpc_year:<year>, at ELEVATED weight scaled by magnitude (major 4 / mid 3 / minor 2).
gpc_seeding.pool_band: Total GPC-thread weight kept between 1/3 (FLOOR) and 2/5 (CAP) of the live thread pool -- canon surfaces with VERY HIGH odds without drowning the player's own arcs.
gpc_seeding.scheduled_vs_surfaced: GPC events still FIRE on the year metronome regardless; the high-weight thread makes them LOOM/recur in oracle moments (rumor, summons, NPC arrival, complication, foreshadowing) before & around the scheduled scene.
gpc_seeding.retire: At year-end, DEMOTE the past year's spent GPC threads to LOW weight (1) -- NOT zero (player direction; softens Ruling #31 for GPC items) -- so their aftermath still recurs.
